name: Monday, Tuesday

attributes.attribute: the only words the fairies sang repeatedly in a folkloric motif
removed a hunch as thanks for the added word Wednesday
added a hump to a rude second hunchback who sang Friday
the second one kept the first man's hump on top of his own

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Monday, Tuesday marks a folkloric motif about the fairies. The fairies loved dancing and singing, but their music was simple. They sang the words Monday, Tuesday over and over, in Irish Da Luan, Da Mart. A hunchback grew irritated with the song. He added the words and Wednesday, in Irish Agus da Cadin, to their tune. The fairies felt great excitement and delight at the new melody. In gratitude they removed the man's hunch, and he walked away straight as an arrow. Another hunchback heard the story. He rushed to the same place and waited for the fairies. As soon as they began to sing, he interrupted them with the words and Friday, in Irish Agus da Hena. The fairies, angry at his rudeness, put the first man's hump on top of his own.
objective: Document the fairies and the Monday, Tuesday motif.
key_results: Record the fairies' song of Monday, Tuesday, in Irish Da Luan, Da Mart.
Record the first hunchback who added Wednesday and lost his hunch.
Record the second hunchback who added Friday and gained a hump.
